extracted.intended_audience: bibliometric researchers, data curators, librarians, and users of OpenAlex and other bibliographic APIs
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and validating how retraction and other update statuses are represented in OpenAlex metadata (and how that representation affects downstream users), and methods for correcting or mitigating misclassifications. Focused on comparing OpenAlex fields to upstream Crossref 'update-nature' data and practical verification workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate representation of publication status
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAlex must represent publication status (retraction, correction, expression of concern, etc.) accurately rather than misclassifying non-retractions as retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crossref provides a granular 'update-nature' field containing Corrections, Expressions of Concern, Crossmark Retractions and more; OpenAlex's sole boolean 'is_retracted' caused misclassifications (e.g., a corrected but not retracted Corman et al. 2020 paper). Evaluate whether a platform's status field faithfully reflects upstream semantics before trusting 'retracted' flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve metadata granularity (avoid collapsing to a boolean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not consolidate multiple distinct update types into a single boolean 'is_retracted' field that conflates corrections, expressions of concern, and retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper highlights that 'the mere presence of any information about an update causes OpenAlex to categorise the publication as retracted.' Systems should retain distinct labels (retraction vs correction vs expression_of_concern) to avoid loss of meaning and downstream harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to upstream sources (use authoritative fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata providers should preserve and surface authoritative upstream fields (e.g., Crossref's 'update-nature') rather than discarding or flattening them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors enriched OpenAlex records with Crossref 'update-nature' to detect misclassifications. When evaluating publication status, prefer canonical upstream fields (Crossref, Retraction Watch) and document how mappings were done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special care for any indication of retraction status
rubrics_metrics.description: Every indication of a retraction status must be subject to special care and verification before being relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors recommend that 'every indication of a retraction status must be subject to special care.' Treat retraction flags as high-risk metadata and verify with primary sources (journal notice, Retraction Watch) before taking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify critical metadata with alternative tools and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-check retraction status using additional resources (e.g., Retraction Watch database, Problematic Paper Screener's Annulled Detector) before using or publishing derived conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper suggests 'subject such critical metadata to a close examination, including with alternative tools for verifying the status of publications,' and provides links to Retraction Watch and the Annulled Detector as examples of verification tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check temporal/versioned data snapshots and API release windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of and check the exact API/data-snapshot time window used, since metadata errors may affect particular snapshot/API-response periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors identify the affected period (metadata via API between 22 Dec 2023 and 19 Mar 2024 and snapshot releases 2024-01-24 and 2024-02-27). Users relying on data from specific dates should urgently re-check and replace affected datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent marking of retractions across databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure retractions are consistently and transparently marked across all reference databases where a publication is indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes 'ensuring consistent marking of retractions across all reference databases ... remains a challenge.' Cross-database inconsistency should trigger further verification before any downstream use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices must be clear and include rationale and date
rubrics_metrics.description: Retracted papers should contain a clear note on the journal website indicating retraction status, the rationale, and the date of retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors describe that 'information about retractions is typically published separately within the journal, where editors explain the rationale behind the decision as well as the date of retraction.' Use these journal notices as authoritative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid information loss from complexity reduction in metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata simplification should not produce loss of crucial information (e.g., conflating update types or dropping explanatory fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper warns that 'complexity reduction in the metadata representation must not lead to a loss of information.' Preserve fields needed to interpret the nature and severity of updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance and reproducibility: use snapshots and share scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use full database snapshots for reproducibility and share scripts/data used for analyses so others can validate findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors used OpenAlex database snapshots and provided their data and scripts at a GitHub repository. This practice supports reproducibility and enables correction tracing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require DOIs (or other persistent identifiers) for reliable enrichment
rubrics_metrics.description: Match and enrich records via DOIs; be cautious or exclude records without DOIs when reconciling retraction/update metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors excluded 704 records lacking DOIs when enriching OpenAlex records with Crossref 'update-nature.' Lack of persistent identifiers complicates reliable cross-mapping and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for limitations of experimental APIs and incomplete datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and document when upstream APIs or experimental endpoints provide incomplete coverage, and treat conclusions accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to the 'experimental character of the Labs API' the authors could not obtain a complete dataset; analyses that rely on such endpoints should include caveats and, where possible, seek more complete sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and use a reporting/correction workflow with data providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish channels to report metadata errors to data providers and follow up to ensure corrections are applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors contacted the OurResearch team, which resulted in ~2300 incorrect records being corrected. Document report submissions, responses, and corrected record identifiers to track remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess downstream impact and prioritize verification of highly cited or clinical papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the potential downstream harm of misclassifications (e.g., highly cited clinical papers) and prioritize verification for items with greater impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper warns that mislabelling influential publications 'has the potential to misinform healthcare professionals and jeopardize patient care.' Prioritize checking high-impact items and those used in clinical or policy contexts.
